description: Sixth converted statistics pass. Adds Hypertext d20-compatible creature stat blocks for Sheffels, Skyflayers, and Flufftrounces.

entries.title: Sheffels
entries.summary: Large, placid herd animals drift through the skies and provide food, hide, transport, and livelihood to sky communities, now with converted Hypertext d20-compatible statistics.
body: Sheffels are buoyant herd beasts adapted to open air and floating-island pasture. Their calm temperament permits domestication and aerial herding, while their bodies supply meat, milk, leather, and other necessities.
Though rarely aggressive, their mass, herd panic, and defensive shoulder rushes can endanger riders, airships, and exposed structures.

sections.heading: Conversion posture
body: Converted as a domesticated aerial livestock animal with herd panic, buoyant movement, and defensive trampling rather than as a combat predator.

statBlocks.title: Sheffel
speed: Fly 50 ft. (average; hover only while lightly loaded)
statBlocks.fullAttack: Headbutt +10 melee (1d8+7) and 2 hoof kicks +5 melee (1d6+3)
specialAttacks: Buoyant Rush (Ex): If a Sheffel flies at least 20 ft. in a straight line before making a headbutt, the attack deals 2d8+10 damage and the target must succeed on a DC 20 Reflex save or be pushed 10 ft.

Herd Panic (Ex): When a Sheffel within 60 ft. is frightened, reduced below half hit points, or killed, each other Sheffel in the herd must succeed on a DC 14 Will save or panic for 1d4 rounds. Panicked Sheffels flee along the herd's direction and make a trample attack against creatures in their path.
Trample (Ex): 1d8+10 damage, Reflex DC 20 half, against Medium or smaller creatures.
statBlocks.environment: Floating-island pasture, open sky ranches, agricultural routes
statBlocks.organization: Solitary, pair, herd (6-40), or managed drove (20-200)
tactics: Avoids conflict and attempts to follow the herd or handler.
Uses Buoyant Rush only when cornered or protecting young.
The real threat in encounters is often herd panic near ships, cliffs, or crowded docks.
conversionNotes: Converted from the source's aerial livestock role, placid temperament, and economic importance.
Designed to support herd, transport, ranching, and environmental encounters as well as combat.

entries.title: Skyflayer
entries.summary: A feared aerial predator uses speed, concealment, and sudden attacks to hunt travelers and flying animals, now with converted Hypertext d20-compatible statistics.
body: Skyflayers are legendary ambush hunters of the open air. They exploit clouds and poor visibility, striking isolated prey before withdrawing into the sky.
Their reputation makes sightings significant to pilots, herders, and settlements whose livestock graze beyond defended airspace.

sections.heading: Conversion posture
body: Converted as a high-speed aerial ambusher whose danger comes from concealment, isolation, and repeated diving attacks rather than prolonged toe-to-toe combat.

statBlocks.title: Skyflayer
specialAttacks: Cloud Ambush (Ex): While in cloud, fog, smoke, rain, or similarly obscured air, the Skyflayer may hide without cover and gains a +10 racial bonus on Hide checks. A target denied its Dexterity bonus to AC takes +4d6 damage from the Skyflayer's first successful attack.

Flaying Dive (Ex): If the Skyflayer descends at least 40 ft. before attacking, both talons deal double damage. If both hit the same target, the target must succeed on a DC 27 Fortitude save or take 1d4 Constitution damage from severe tearing wounds.

Snatch and Drop (Ex): Against Large or smaller targets, a successful talon hit permits a free grapple attempt. If the Skyflayer begins its turn airborne while holding a target, it may ascend up to half speed and release the target as a free action.
Predator's Shriek (Su): 90-ft. cone once every 1d4 rounds; creatures must succeed on a DC 21 Will save or become shaken for 1d6 rounds. Isolated creatures take a -4 penalty on this save.
statBlocks.environment: Cloud banks, isolated aerial routes, remote grazing skies
statBlocks.treasure: Incidental remains and equipment carried from prey
tactics: Stalks travelers from cloud cover and attacks the most isolated target.
Uses Flaying Dive, then climbs back into concealment rather than remaining in melee.
Carries vulnerable prey away from allies and drops heavily armored targets.
conversionNotes: Converted from the source's speed, concealment, and sudden aerial attack identity.
Built to reward formation discipline and cloud visibility management.

entries.title: Flufftrounce
entries.summary: A harmless winged rabbit-like creature disperses seeds and is valued as a companion and source of delicate fur, now with converted Hypertext d20-compatible statistics.
body: Flufftrounces travel in small herds between islands, feeding on airborne plants, fruit, insects, and spores. Their buoyant wings and nervous bursts of speed make them difficult to catch.
Their fur leaves a drifting cloud, and their movements distribute plant life across isolated habitats.

sections.heading: Conversion posture
body: Converted as a harmless evasive companion animal and ecological utility creature rather than a combatant.

statBlocks.title: Flufftrounce
specialAttacks: Startle Burst (Ex): When first threatened or when an adjacent creature makes a sudden loud noise, the Flufftrounce may immediately move up to half its fly speed without provoking attacks of opportunity. It may use this once per round.

Fur Cloud (Ex): Once per minute, the Flufftrounce may shed a 10-ft.-radius cloud of fine fur and spores lasting 1 round. Creatures inside gain concealment, but must succeed on a DC 11 Fortitude save or be dazzled for 1 round from sneezing and watery eyes.
statBlocks.environment: Flowering floating islands, orchard routes, quiet cloud meadows
statBlocks.levelAdjustment: +1 as an improved familiar or companion
tactics: Avoids all combat and flees in unpredictable vertical bursts.
Uses Fur Cloud to break line of sight and hide among plants or rigging.
Domesticated individuals return to trusted handlers once danger passes.
conversionNotes: Converted from the source's harmless aerial rabbit, evasive movement, fur cloud, and seed-dispersal role.
Suitable as an improved familiar, pet, ecological encounter, or low-stakes chase objective.
